text:
alex: quick note — after yesterday's burst we got paged for 23 GPU p95 spikes across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. thinking we need a new routing + suppression approach to cut noise

maya: yep saw that. most were single-sample blips from scheduled job churn, not cluster degradation. cost of wakeups is high (alerts + oncall context switch).

dom: can we share the query? i suspect our current rule pages on short p95 blips.

alex: current rule (simplified):
```promql
avg_over_instances(gpu_latency_p95{job="inference"}) > 1.5
```
for: 1m

alex: proposal: 3 changes — 1) require persistence (for: 5m) 2) add cardinality gating (only page if affected nodes >= 4 or affected pools >= 2) 3) downgrade single-node/single-pool to ticket with high priority.

maya: sounds good. also add region-awareness — don't page eu and us at the same time unless they both meet thresholds. reduces duplicate paging for global fanouts.

sam: +1. also recommend grouping key = cluster_name + gpu_pool so alerts aggregate nicely in ops console.

lee: can we embed an SLI check? e.g., if routing affects customers above SLO (error budget burn or 99th request latency for customer-facing requests) then always page. otherwise ticket.

dom: agree. so final decision path:
- if SLI breach OR sustained > 5m AND (node_cardinality >= 4 OR pool_cardinality >=2) => page
- else if sustained > 2m but low cardinality => auto-create ticket with alert annotations and annotated dashboard link
- else => metric-only annotation (no page/ticket)

alex: here's a proposed PromQL snippet for the page rule (draft):
```promql
(sum by(cluster_name, gpu_pool) (increase(gpu_latency_p95{job="inference"}[5m]) > 0) >= 4)
and avg_over_time(gpu_latency_p95[5m]) > 1.5
```
for: 5m

maya: minor nit — use `count_values` or `count by (node)` to accurately count impacted nodes. the increase() part might mislead.

sam: operational notes: 1) add a mute-window between 02:00-03:30 local cluster time for batch window restarts 2) run the new config in canary for 48h in staging and eu-west-1 prod with oncall notifications routed to an experiment channel 3) add auto-escalation if ticket not acknowledged within 60m.

oncall-bot: alert-change-requested: new rule will be deployed to canary channel at 2026-04-05T04:00Z. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-p95-playbook

lee: also record cost estimate: every pager averages ~40m of engineer time (context + mitigation) = ~$250. cutting false pages from 23->3/day saves ~20hrs/day. we should add that to PR description.

dom: i'll draft the PR with test dashboards and a short eval harness (replay last 30 days to simulate pages). can we add a label `alert_experiment: p95-cardinality-v1` for easy rollback?

alex: yes. and add an annotation `observability_pr: <PR_LINK>` so we can track.

maya: one more — expose the grouping in Grafana alerting UI so SRE can mute specific pools without muting a whole region.

sam: plan approved by channel. next steps: dom opens PR + replay test, run 48h canary in eu-west-1, meet after canary with metric: pages/day, tickets created, MTTR, false-positive rate.

lee: I'll prepare a short SLO scoreboard panel for the post-mortem.

dom: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/314 — tagging you all. will flip to canary tomorrow.

alex: thanks everyone. we'll iterate on thresholds after the replay results. :thumbsup:
